podcast.body: A seminal moment for hip-hop culture in the mainstream, "Rapture" began climbing the charts while "The Tide Is High" was still at number one. It featured a bizarre rap break penned by Chris Stein and Debbie Harry, shouting out Fab 5 Freddy and Grandmaster Flash, and telling a "loopy tale of a man from Mars eating cars." Keyboardist Jimmy Destry added tubular bells, and the rhythm section contributed a post-disco groove. It quickly reached number one just eight weeks after its debut, completing Blondie's "quad-fecta" of number one songs in four different styles between 1979 and 1981, and also peaked at number 33 on Billboard's Soul Singles chart. "Just eight weeks after it debuted, Rapture was number one."
